content.value_statement: dbt projects can become inconsistent as models, tests, and documentation grow. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear patterns for model layers, naming, tests, docs, and incremental builds.
actual_capabilities: Explains staging, intermediate, and marts model layers for dbt projects.
Provides naming conventions for staging models, intermediate models, dimensions, and facts.
Shows source definitions, freshness settings, and column-level tests.
Demonstrates dbt model SQL for staging, intermediate, dimension, and fact tables.
Covers macros, incremental strategies, documentation files, and common dbt commands.
limitations: Does not inspect a live warehouse or validate SQL against real schemas.
Does not generate adapter-specific optimizations for every warehouse.
Requires users to adapt sample model names, schemas, and tests to their data.
Does not replace project-specific governance, privacy, or access controls.

use_cases.title: Structure a New dbt Project
use_cases.description: Create a clear folder layout, model layer plan, and naming approach before transformation work starts.

use_cases.title: Improve Analytics Models
use_cases.description: Refactor staging, intermediate, dimension, and fact models using consistent transformation patterns.

use_cases.title: Standardize Quality Practices
use_cases.description: Define documentation, freshness checks, relationship tests, and accepted values across shared dbt models.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a dbt Project Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a dbt project structure for these sources and analytics goals. Include model layers, folders, naming rules, and first tests.

prompt_templates.title: Create Staging Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these raw source tables into dbt staging model guidance. Include source definitions, renamed fields, freshness checks, and column tests.

prompt_templates.title: Design Marts and Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design dbt dimension and fact models for this business process. Include upstream dependencies, metrics, grain, tests, and documentation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Incremental Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this dbt incremental model plan. Recommend the best incremental strategy, unique keys, late-arriving data handling, and validation tests.

output_examples.input: Organize a new dbt project for Stripe payments and Shopify orders.
output_examples.output: A layered plan with sources, staging, intermediate, and marts folders, plus naming rules for each model group.

output_examples.input: Improve tests for customer and order marts.
output_examples.output: A test coverage checklist covering unique keys, not-null checks, relationships, accepted values, recency, and value bounds.

output_examples.input: Choose an incremental strategy for a large events table.
output_examples.output: A recommendation comparing merge, delete-and-insert, and partition overwrite based on late data, table size, and warehouse support.

best_practices: Start with source definitions, freshness checks, and staging models before building marts.
Document model grain, important columns, and business logic near the models.
Pair each critical transformation with unique, not-null, relationship, or accepted-value tests.
anti_patterns: Do not build marts directly from raw source tables without a staging layer.
Do not hardcode project dates, schemas, or business logic that should be variables or macros.
Do not choose incremental materialization before defining unique keys and late-data behavior.

faq.question: What kind of dbt work does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports model organization, source definitions, tests, documentation, macros, and incremental transformation planning.

faq.question: Can it run dbt commands for me?
faq.answer: It lists standard dbt commands, but users must decide when to run commands in their own environment.

faq.question: Does it support data quality testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes uniqueness, not-null, relationship, accepted-value, recency, and expression-based tests.

faq.question: Is this tied to one data warehouse?
faq.answer: No. The patterns are general dbt guidance, but adapter-specific SQL may require changes.

faq.question: Can it help with incremental models?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares common strategies and shows how to plan keys, filters, and schema change handling.

faq.question: Does it replace a project review?
faq.answer: No. Teams should still review warehouse permissions, data privacy rules, and production deployment controls.
